extracted.intended_audience: federal agency managers and staff responsible for preparing Annual Management Reports under OMB Circular A-44 (e.g., program managers, planning/programming/budget offices, inspectors general)
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare the Annual Management Report called for by OMB Circular A-44 (Management Review and Improvement Program), documenting management reviews, priority improvement projects, financial accomplishments/plans, productivity and cost-reduction measures, and nominees for management-improvement awards, and submit in the prescribed format and by assigned deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / focus on operating program contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of this Circular is to provide guidelines for management review and management improvements that will focus agency efforts on operating programs and on the functions essential to their support. These efforts will be evaluated at all levels based on contributions made to achieving operating program objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize contributions to operating program objectives rather than producing an impressive report; identify and achieve measurable improvements in program management, productivity, evaluation and performance that benefit the Agency and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of operating programs for mission impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination of operating programs to ascertain their impact on accomplishing a significant aspect of the overall mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how each operating program materially advances the agency's mission; prioritize reviews on programs with significant mission impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appraisal for efficiency and effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Appraisal of operations to determine whether they are performed efficiently and effectively and to identify alternative approaches for performing them in a more cost-effective manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider alternative methods, processes, or organizational changes that can improve efficiency, effectiveness and cost-effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess need/function relative to mission
rubrics_metrics.description: The need for a program or function in terms of its contribution to accomplishing the mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Question whether ongoing activities are necessary or could be reduced/terminated based on mission relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-effectiveness of proposed improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost-effectiveness of an improvement in terms of the potential benefits to be obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh benefits against costs; improvements should show a favorable benefit-to-cost rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of resources and priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The availability of resources to apply to the proposed improvement in terms of department or agency-wide priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether resources (funds, personnel, time) are available and consistent with higher-level priorities before proposing implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for initiatives encouraging better resource use
rubrics_metrics.description: The opportunity presented by an improvement for new initiatives that will encourage greater use of resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor improvements that enable more effective or innovative use of existing resources across the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance indicators: productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Use productivity indicators (example: applications processed per man-year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish baseline and target productivity measures; use numeric targets and track changes year-to-year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance indicators: service
rubrics_metrics.description: Use service indicators (example: average total processing time per application in days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure timeliness and service-level targets; report current and target service metrics for comparative assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance indicators: quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Use quality indicators (example: percent of applications requiring reprocessing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track rework/error rates or other quality metrics and set improvement targets (multiple-year comparisons encouraged).

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance indicators: cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Use cost indicators (example: unit cost per application in dollars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report unit costs with baseline and target values; link cost indicators to productivity, service, and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish objectives and multiple performance indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishment of objectives and performance indicators with emphasis on multiple indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a balanced set of indicators (productivity, service, quality, cost) rather than relying on a single metric; set objectives for current and future years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify management problem areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify management problem areas as the first step in change of approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct systematic reviews to surface problem areas before selecting improvement projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select priority improvement projects (emphasize operating programs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of priority improvement projects with emphasis on operating program areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize projects that most directly affect operating programs and agency mission; focus scarce resources on highest-priority initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assign implementation responsibility to program managers
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation responsibility assigned to program managers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold program managers accountable for executing improvement projects rather than leaving implementation solely to central management staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate accomplishments by contribution to operating objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Accomplishments evaluated in terms of contribution to achievement of operating program objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess success by measurable contribution to program goals (productivity, service, quality, cost) rather than by administrative outputs alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management reviews: methods and instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a range of review methods: guidance, idea interchange, interagency coordination, assessment, on-site surveys, interagency studies, annual management reports, management issues reviews, plans/accomplishments tracking, budget hearings, annual management letters, consultants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ multiple tools and interagency coordination as appropriate; schedule on-site surveys and assessments to gather substantive evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Management Report contents — Section I: Management reviews (accomplishments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section I should cover Management Effectiveness Accomplishments (e.g., new procedures, reductions in backlog, savings achieved).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document specific actions taken, measurable achievements, and quantitative savings where possible (e.g., reduction in reports, backlog decreases, percent reductions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Management Report contents — Section II: Priority improvement projects (cost reduction accomplishments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section II should report Cost Reduction Accomplishments and priority improvement projects undertaken in the fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show project descriptions, actions taken, and computed savings (dollar and operational impacts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Management Report contents — Section III: Financial accomplishments and plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Section III should present Financial Accomplishments and Plans (budgetary implications, savings goals, and financial projections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include baseline cost figures, savings goals, and actual savings achieved; tie financial data to program objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Management Report contents — Section IV: Automatic data processing / ADP plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Section IV should cover Automatic Data Processing (ADP) matters (plans and projects involving automation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe ADP objectives, expected benefits (efficiency, reduction in personnel/paper files), and projected impacts on service, productivity and cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Management Report contents — Section V: Management of Federal reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Section V should address Management of Federal Reports (efforts to reduce reporting requirements and related paperwork).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a Report Reduction Report with base period counts/costs, savings goals, and actual savings by reporting category (public, interagency, internal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Management Report contents — Section VI: Productivity improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Section VI should document Productivity Improvements (measures and projects that raised productivity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report productivity metrics (e.g., applications per man-year) with year-to-year comparisons and targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Management Report contents — Section VII: Cost reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Section VII should document Cost Reductions (actions and quantified savings achieved).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide dollar savings, methods used to obtain reductions, and sustainability of savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Management Report contents — Section VIII: Nominees for Presidential Management Improvement Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Section VIII should list Nominees for Presidential Management Improvement Awards and related personnel recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit nominees via personnel offices as prescribed; include accomplishments supporting nomination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report significance and validity over quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: Report only those accomplishments and plans which are reasonably significant in terms of achieving some Agency management, operational or cost reduction goal; the quality and validity of reported items are more important than quantity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reported accomplishments bear up under scrutiny and plans reflect serious intentions; suggest priority improvement projects requiring Agency-wide attention where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to OMB-prescribed format and exhibit
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Section must be prepared in accordance with the format prescribed by OMB in the Attachment and the Exhibit to Circular A-44 (Revised); self-designed forms or formats will be returned for re-submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the exact OMB Attachment/Exhibit structure, labeling sections as required; do not submit nonstandard formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of baseline/current/target year comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Present performance indicators with base year, past year, current year and target year values (e.g., productivity, service, quality, cost across FY1971–FY1973).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report numeric baselines and multi-year targets to show trends and objectives; include both past performance and future goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadlines and assignment of section responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow assigned deadlines and office responsibilities for preparing sections (e.g., Inspector General responsible for Section I; Director of Finance for Section III; Director of Personnel for Section VIII; Directorate contributions due by specified dates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate internally to meet OMB due date (Agency-integrated report due to OMB by 1 September 1972 in this instance) and intermediate office deadlines; submit through designated channels.
